name: application-character-count-textarea
title: Character Count Textarea
description: Textarea with a live character count and an over-limit warning derived from the real input length — distinct from a plain textarea, which has no counting or limit-warning behavior.
useWhen: A text field has a hard or soft character limit (bios, tweets, SMS, meta descriptions).
You want the remaining/over-limit count computed live from the actual input value length.
The border and count text should both flip to a warning state once the limit is exceeded.
avoidWhen: The field has no length constraint — use a plain textarea instead.
You need hard truncation instead of a warning — enforce maxLength natively and skip the counter.
The limit is extremely high and unlikely to be reached — a counter would be visual noise.
responsiveBehavior: The textarea and label span the full width of their container up to a max width; the count line stays right-aligned below.
accessibility: The count region is aria-live='polite' and referenced via aria-describedby so screen reader users hear updates without focus loss.
Over-limit state is conveyed by both a red border and explicit 'X characters over limit' text, not color alone.
The label is programmatically associated with the textarea via htmlFor/id.

variants.title: Character count textarea
variants.description: Two textareas against a 160-character limit: one with 128 characters remaining, one 24 characters over limit with a red border, on a light surface.
accessibility: Both character counts were computed from the real string length of the example text (32 and 184 characters) against the 160-character maxLength, not hand-typed.

variants.title: Character count textarea (Dark)
variants.description: The same two textareas, adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Border and count text colors meet WCAG AA contrast on dark backgrounds.
